_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_session: SkyPort, Session 216 — the one-pool model shipped
_status: The adopted one-pool model is BUILT into the live Implementation Funding tab and every test is green: $25.24M over all 118 institutions, $150K base to $400K cap on the combined award, every award split into credit and noncredit shares, the three noncredit-only campuses earning by origination. Sam ran three reaction rounds live (collapsible sections, centered columns, the statute verbatim behind each goal card, his Summary wording, Draft memo and Save as PDF buttons, an Internal/Public preview, the metric on each priority card's face, LA Southwest and Riverside City) and all of it is in. The pull request was awaiting its final automated check at checkpoint time; merging it publishes the tab. Next up: the origination data feed (the three noncredit-only campuses draw nothing until it flows) and one display decision for Sam.

items.text: One display call is yours: in Annual funding view an award cell can read 'earning $140,476 · 191%' because the earning shown is the whole two-year window while the figure beside it is one year's. The code does this on purpose (earning is a window quantity) but two independent reviewers read it as over-earning. Say the word and the percent will be computed against the window figure instead, which never exceeds 100%.

The MAP Custom Reports origination instructions for Malone and Pedro are ready to forward (Word doc delivered in chat; also filed in the vault). It formalizes the Origin + LocID2 plan Pedro has held since 8-26. The tab is now BUILT to consume this feed with no further code change — but no funding moves to NOCE, SDCCE, or Calbright until it flows, so the column spellings from Malone/Pedro are the one thing holding the trio's earn-out.

The SS75013 workgroup seat (your yes, 2026-08-30, item 9): pursue it in collaboration with CO Governmental Relations, CO Finance, and the Department of Finance - the CBE-to-FTES funding measure that reports to Finance by October 2028 is register row #7's named obstacle being designed. A session can draft the outreach note whenever you want it.

Memo A ('what is already law') is drafted and lives IN the GR tab now - open Guidance memos under the CPL area, edit any section, and Export memo (Word) uses the register's generator (the hold banner and drafting annex travel in the file until status says issued). Your sequencing ruling holds: BOG adoption first, then issuance. One external confirm before issuance: the section-2 accreditation-standards claim needs an ACCJC touchpoint. Memo B and C stubs sit beside it when you want them drafted.

One one-click finish left (2026-08-30): review and merge the public KB's draft PR #22 (the Rule 8 -> Rule 9 renumber, two files) - your merge IS the curation gate. (The experiment-branch deletion is DONE and verified.)

Run the context-pressure installer so sessions warn you before they run out of room: pull main, then `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install-context-hook.ps1`. Until it is installed nothing warns — which is how we lost 778,000 tokens of working context on the 29th. Tell us if it errors; it could not be tested from the agent side.

End every scoring sitting on your testing bench with 'Show the log as text' and paste it into a working session — one paste files everything durably in the vault. Until you export, scores live only in that browser and a cleared browser eats them.

Two finishes on the shipped one-pool tab: (1) if PR #1427 is still open, merge it once its automated test check passes — that publishes the new tab; (2) when Malone/Pedro confirm the origination columns' exact spellings, flip the performance builder's cutover so the feed flows — the tab itself needs no further change, the tests prove it.

Two small polish jobs left behind by the port: (1) the college briefing still shows internal short names ('LA Swest', 'Riverside') where the funding tab now says LA Southwest and Riverside City — sweeping it belongs with the college-and-district identity work so every surface renames once, consistently; (2) a cleanup commit for ~15 styling rules serving row shapes that no longer exist plus one frozen-header selector naming a retired row class. Nothing visible moves; it keeps future sessions from chasing ghosts.

Sam's yes (2026-08-30, item 10): run the sixteen-row register sweep once on the small model - the hardest thing Sierra does - and report what it caught versus the last full-model run. Sequencing: run it BEFORE the register verdicts rewrite rows, so both models are compared on the same ground. Revert immediately if it disappoints, else when corporate billing lands; the revert is one Supabase config setting, no code change.

The rule-testing groundwork is DONE (2026-08-30): the committed criteria were re-checked against the current rulebook with notes recorded beside them, and the redo recipe for the control-arm comparison is written — all filed in the vault. What remains is running the sittings themselves, on demand from the bench; results file into the vault, never here.

One file is rebuilt daily by a scheduled job but never committed by it, so the published copy goes stale: the pathways dataset. Small mechanical fix when someone wants it. (The second file originally listed here was re-checked and cleared - the job everyone suspected never actually rewrites it; the one that does also publishes it.)

Sweep the other curator tabs for three save faults found on the funding tab: a page that only accepts the team password locks out someone signed in by magic link; edits made before signing in can stay stranded in the browser while looking saved; and a tab may still offer editing that the database would refuse. Decide per tab whether it should require a personal sign-in like the funding tab now does.

The memory table has no consistency check at all, so a saved note can say the opposite of the standing rules and nothing notices. This is one of only two known failures nothing catches; the other is that our document checker cannot see the Obsidian vault, so it cannot tell a skipped update from one that never applied.
